title: Foam Whale Nativity Attachment
subject: Civil Procedure
stem:
At a privately rented Bible-story obstacle-course party in State A, Lydia and Daniel, both State A citizens, are helping set up a giant foam whale prop. Daniel negligently bumps the prop, which falls and injures Lydia. Daniel owns a hand-carved olive-wood Nativity set stored in a private storage locker in State B, but Daniel has no other contacts with State B. Lydia sues Daniel in a State B court for the prop injury and attaches the Nativity set, arguing that the property gives State B power to decide the whole injury claim.

What is the best analysis?

choices.A: State B may decide the claim because Lydia was injured, and plaintiffs choose the forum.
choices.B: State B likely lacks personal jurisdiction over the unrelated prop-injury claim despite the attached Nativity set.
choices.C: State B has jurisdiction only if the Nativity set is valuable enough to satisfy the whole judgment.
choices.D: State B may decide the entire injury claim because any property in the forum creates personal jurisdiction.

rightExplanation: B is the best analysis. Gold Key: Attaching a defendant’s forum property does not itself let the forum decide an unrelated personal claim; after Shaffer, the property must supply a jurisdictional connection among the defendant, the forum, and the litigation, or other minimum contacts must exist. Silver Key: Lock the call as court power, not collection. The attached asset is only a lure unless it connects to the claim.

c3.label: CUT A
c3.text: Not responsive. Plaintiff injury and forum choice do not answer the court-power question.

c3.label: CUT C
c3.text: Not responsive. Asset value answers judgment satisfaction, not jurisdiction.

c3.label: CUT D
c3.text: Not true by Gold Key. “Any property” is an overclaim; unrelated property alone is not enough.

c3.label: CALL
c3.text: Not needed beyond the Gold Key anchor.

studentScript: Call is State B power over Daniel. A is plaintiff choice, not defendant contact. C is collection value, not court power. D says any property, but Gold Key says unrelated property is not enough. B remains.

A.signal: The answer talks about Lydia's injury and forum choice, but the call asks whether State B has power over Daniel.
A.lawyer: A plaintiff's choice of forum does not create personal jurisdiction over a defendant.

B.signal: It answers the exact court-power question and uses the property/claim mismatch.
B.lawyer: Under Shaffer, unrelated forum property alone does not support jurisdiction absent other ties among defendant, forum, and litigation.

C.signal: Value of the attached item answers collection, not court power.
C.lawyer: The due-process problem is lack of jurisdictional connection, not the amount of attached property.

D.signal: The word any turns property presence into an unlimited court-power rule.
D.lawyer: Shaffer rejects jurisdiction based solely on unrelated forum property.

goldKeys.statement: Forum property is not a magic key. If the claim is unrelated to the attached property, the forum still needs a defendant-forum-litigation connection.
goldKeys.trigger: A plaintiff attaches a defendant's forum property to sue on an unrelated personal claim.
goldKeys.authority: Shaffer v. Heitner, 433 U.S. 186; International Shoe Co. v. Washington, 326 U.S. 310.

silverKeys.statement: Separate court power from collection. An asset's value may matter after a valid judgment, but it does not answer whether this court can decide the claim.
silverKeys.trigger: An answer asks whether the attached property can satisfy the whole judgment.

remediation.title: Unrelated property is not forum power.
remediation.signal: Plaintiff attaches defendant's forum property for a claim arising elsewhere.
remediation.studentMove: Ask whether the property connects the defendant, forum, and litigation.
remediation.tinyRule: Unrelated property alone does not create jurisdiction over the personal claim.
